# Jobwatch MCP App (mcp-use, TypeScript)

A thin MCP Apps front for the Jobwatch ChatGPT connector. It holds no job data and no safety logic.
Every tool calls the Python JSON front `pipeline/agentic/connector_http.py` (loopback, bearer), which calls the same
`chatgpt_connector` functions the live Python MCP service uses. The digest check, single-use approvals,
per-person binding and "already queued" refusal all stay in Python.

## Tools
<!-- tool-reference:start (generated by `npm run docs`; edit src/tools.ts instead) -->
24 tools for the model, 2 app-only buttons (generated from `src/tools.ts`).

| Tool | Group | Effect | Opens a view | Use when | Not for | Next |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jobwatch_guide` | guide | read-only | never | you are unsure what to do next, how an approval works, or after an error | pasting at the person; use it to act and explain in your own words | act on it, e.g. onboarding_status or jobs_overview |
| `onboarding_status` | onboarding | read-only | never | first in a new conversation, or when setup is unclear | asking the person anything yourself; you run the conversation | ask the open questions, review_onboarding when none remain, discovery_status when confirmed |
| `start_onboarding` | onboarding | writes | never | onboarding_status says not_started and you have upload_ids | a draft already exists, or inventing document IDs | onboarding_status until parsing ends, then ask the saved questions yourself |
| `update_onboarding` | onboarding | writes | never | the person states or corrects a profile fact | saving anything the person did not say; never invent facts | onboarding_status for remaining questions, then review_onboarding |
| `answer_onboarding_question` | onboarding | writes | never | the person has answered a saved onboarding question | answering for the person, or confirming the profile | more questions via onboarding_status, or review_onboarding when none remain |
| `review_onboarding` | onboarding | read-only | never | no open questions remain and the person should confirm their profile | confirming; show the review to the person and wait for their yes | confirm_onboarding with these unchanged digests after the person's explicit yes |
| `confirm_onboarding` | onboarding | writes | never | the person clearly said yes to what review_onboarding returned | any consent you inferred or any changed draft | discovery_status |
| `discovery_status` | discovery | read-only | never | the person asks if it is working, why nothing is new, or what failed | recommending jobs; collected postings are not recommendations | jobs_overview, or start_discovery / retry_assessment only on request |
| `start_discovery` | discovery | writes | never | the person wants more jobs assessed now | retrying a failure (retry_assessment) or refreshing the shortlist (refresh_shortlist) | discovery_status for the real progress; queued is not done |
| `retry_assessment` | discovery | writes | never | the person explicitly asks to retry that failed assessment | retrying on your own, or raising spending limits | discovery_status to see whether it succeeded |
| `get_discovery_settings` | settings | read-only | never | the person asks how much it can spend | changing the allowance (set_discovery_settings) | set_discovery_settings only if the person asks to change it |
| `set_discovery_settings` | settings | writes | never | the person explicitly asks to change the allowance | changing it on your own | get_discovery_settings to confirm |
| `refresh_shortlist` | shortlist | writes | never | jobs_overview says not_built or stale, or the person asks to refresh | finding new jobs (start_discovery) | jobs_overview |
| `jobs_overview` | shortlist | read-only | never | the person asks what jobs match them or what to apply to | application history, collected postings or assessment activity | job_detail for one entry's evidence; refresh_shortlist if stale |
| `job_detail` | shortlist | read-only | never | recommending a job or answering whether to apply | a job not on the shortlist; assessment_detail is for explicit diagnostics only | ask the person, then prepare_application |
| `assessment_detail` | shortlist | read-only | never | the person explicitly asks why a job was assessed, excluded or failed | picking or recommending jobs (jobs_overview) | explain the reason; discovery_status for failures and retries |
| `applications_overview` | applications | read-only | never | the person asks what they applied to or what needs them on an application | deciding what to apply to (jobs_overview) | task_status or application_detail for one posting |
| `application_detail` | applications | read-only | never | the person asks where their application for a job stands | whether to apply (job_detail) | task_status for progress, review_submission if a draft is ready |
| `task_status` | applications | read-only | never | the person asks how a job's application is going, or to poll after preparing | judging fit (job_detail) | review_submission when it says draft ready |
| `prepare_application` | applications | writes | never | the person explicitly confirmed preparing this job | assessing a job, or changing a draft (revise_application) | task_status until draft ready |
| `revise_application` | applications | writes | never | the person wants something in the CV, letter or answers changed | a first draft (prepare_application) | show the approval, then approve_application |
| `approve_application` | applications | writes | never | the person has seen the approval summary and digest and answered | inventing the quote or answering for the person | task_status for progress |
| `review_submission` | applications | read-only | Submit review | the person asks to review or submit a ready draft | submitting; the person presses Submit themselves | show every answer and document, then revise_application for changes |
| `open_dashboard` | view | read-only | only when asked | the person asks to open the dashboard, widget or view | answering a normal question; use the text tools instead | answer from the text summary if no view appears; jobs_overview for details |

App-only buttons (hidden from the model; only a rendered view may call them):

| Tool | Group | Effect | Opens a view | Use when | Not for | Next |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `decide` | applications | writes | never | never by the model | any model call | approve_application |
| `submit_reviewed` | applications | destructive | never | never by the model | any model call | task_status |

## Host guidance and widgets
- The server sends `instructions` on initialize (operating protocol, generated from the tool registry and `guidance/`), a read-only `jobwatch_guide` tool and `skill://jobwatch/<name>/SKILL.md` resources. See [GUIDANCE.md](GUIDANCE.md).
- Every tool result has a compact text summary (never a JSON dump), the structured data and `next_actions`. A host never needs to render anything.
- Widgets are text-first: no data tool attaches a view. `open_dashboard` is the only tool that opens the interactive view (when the person asks), and `review_submission` carries the Submit review view because it is the person's Submit boundary.
- `JOBWATCH_MCP_WIDGETS=on_request` (default) or `off`. With `off` there is no `open_dashboard`, no view anywhere, and the person submits in Jobwatch's own app.
- The client's declared MCP-Apps support (`io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`) is only used to word hints (`host_views` in `open_dashboard`); behaviour never depends on it.
- `npm run docs` regenerates `src/generated/guidance-bundle.ts` and the tool reference above; the tests fail if they are stale.

## Safety
- `approve_application` answers one pending `revise_application` approval through the same pending approval, person check, expiry, single use and checkpoint as the app-only `decide` (Python `approve_in_chat` calls `decide`). It adds a digest derived from the pending approval (not the secret binding) that Python shows with the approval, and a non-empty `user_quote`. Python cannot verify that a person typed the quote; that trust rests on the host, as for `confirm_onboarding`. Submit approvals are never pending and `submit_reviewed` stays app-only.
- The coordinating assistant owns onboarding conversation and collects the person's answers and consent. Onboarding tools call canonical intake operations directly; they do not start a second chat agent or require widget approval. Only call `confirm_onboarding` after the person explicitly approves the reviewed profile and scope. The backend requires `confirmed: true`, validates both digests under the canonical locks, saves the confirmed version and enables its discovery scope. This does not authorise document preparation, employer messages or application submission. Canonical selection and its durable worker remain responsible for heavy application preparation.
- Submit needs the confirm digest of the reviewed form AND the `shown_hash` of exactly what the review showed (answers, documents, digest); Python refuses `review_changed` if either differs, and does not offer Submit when the owner edited the live form after the fill (`edited_in_browser`). Answers shown are read from the CURRENT live form (the native browser review, same source as the web app); an edit after the fill is re-reviewed and Submit needs the fresh hash. The web process still re-checks the live form before pressing.
- Submit needs the confirm digest of the reviewed form. The view gets it from `_meta` (view-only data) and passes it
  to `submit_reviewed`; Python re-checks it against the live reviewed form and queues once.
- Residual risk: `_meta` is not model-visible by MCP Apps convention, but a host may still forward it to the model.
  Even then the model could only replay `submit_reviewed` with a digest for a form the person has already reviewed;
  hosts hide app-only tools from the model, and Python still refuses a changed form or a second press.
- Authentication is handled by Cloudflare Access Managed OAuth with the configured Google identity provider.
  The tunnel's `originRequest.access.required` setting validates Access JWTs before forwarding to this loopback-only app.
  The app does not ask for a Jobwatch bearer token or passphrase. Keep port 18942 bound to `127.0.0.1` and publish it
  only through the Access-protected tunnel hostname.
- Never run write tools against real data in tests: use `test/mock-backend.mjs`.

## Run (local, mock backend)
    . test/env.sh                      # fake tokens
    node test/mock-backend.mjs &       # port 18941
    npx mcp-use dev --port 18942       # inspector at /mcp/inspector; add header Authorization: Bearer <token>
    npm run build                      # embeds JS/CSS in the MCP View resource for protected deployments
    npm test                           # spawns its own server on 18943

## Real backend
    JOBWATCH_CONNECTOR_TOKEN=... python -m pipeline.agentic.connector_http --port 18940   # JOBWATCH_MCP_PERSON picks the person
    JOBWATCH_MCP_TOKEN=... JOBWATCH_CONNECTOR_TOKEN=... JOBWATCH_BACKEND_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18940 npx mcp-use start --port <port>

## Discovery configuration

Daily token allowance is per person: `get_discovery_settings` reads it and
`set_discovery_settings` saves a positive limit or `daily_token_ceiling: null` for
Unlimited. The separate Discovery panel reads collection and assessment progress,
paused reasons and notification delivery state (delivered, pending, failed, no channel); it can refresh or start discovery when a
confirmed scope is enabled. Status polling does not replace unsaved allowance edits. Individual job/run limits, failure pauses and historical
spending remain.

## Real-application check (temp dir only)
    python -m tests.realapp serve --root /tmp/opencode/realapp --connector-port 18952 --native-port 18951   # real fill + browser; prints the token
    JOBWATCH_REAL_APP_TEST=1 JOBWATCH_PYTHON=<venv python> npx vitest run test/realapp.test.ts
